title: Containerisation
body:
**Containerisation** packages an application with its dependencies and its runtime so it
executes identically wherever it is run. The project used Docker, with a Dockerfile pinning the
Python version and the dependency set.

The problem it solves is that an application depends on far more than its own source: a
language version, library versions, system packages and environment variables. A project that
runs on the author's machine and fails on a marker's differs in one of those, and finding out
which costs more time than the assignment did.

```
Dockerfile        the recipe: base image, dependencies, how to start
image             the built result, identical everywhere
container         a running instance of the image
```

The build is reproducible, so the same Dockerfile produces the same environment months later,
which matters for a project meant to be handed in and read.

It relates directly to [[OPERATING SYSTEMS]]. A container is process isolation built from
kernel features, so it shares the host kernel and starts in milliseconds where a virtual
machine boots an entire operating system. The isolation is namespaces and control groups
applied to a process, which is the kernel providing separation in the same sense it provides a
private [[Address Space]] to every process.
